candidates: When modifying YAML content (e.g., Markdown frontmatter in the docs pipeline), never append or extend it via string concatenation or `+=`. Always parse the existing YAML into a structured object first (e.g., `load()` from `js-yaml` or `parseDocument()` from `yaml`), apply changes to the parsed object, then re-serialize (e.g., `dump()` or `String()`). Appending raw strings to existing YAML produces invalid documents whenever the existing content uses block or flow style.

When adding new YAML-processing code to the project, prefer the `yaml` package over `js-yaml`; `js-yaml` has known quirks (e.g., default schema type coercions, surprising implicit type handling) that are easy to misuse. If `js-yaml` is already imported in a file it is acceptable to reuse it, but new YAML-handling code should default to `yaml`.
